title: EGA VI. Plans, notations, problèmes ouverts : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a working table of contents for a projected chapter of the EGA, labelled here 'EGA VI'. It differs from the plan announced in EGA I (1960), where descent and general construction techniques were assigned to chapter VI. The plan has two parts.

Part A, 'Descente et passage au quotient' (descent and passage to the quotient):
- §1 Faithfully flat descent, as in SGA 1 VIII and FGA 'Technique de descente I'.
- §2 Topologies on (Sch)/S and general properties of functors on (Sch)/S. This replaces a crossed-out 'Passage aux quotients'. In modern terms: fpqc/fppf/étale topologies, sheaves, and algebraic properties such as 'locally of finite presentation', meaning the functor commutes with filtered inductive limits of rings. A marginal query asks whether to insert 'Interventions 1 et 2'.
- §3 Passage to the quotient by flat equivalence relations or groupoids (SGA 3 V; FGA 'Technique de descente III').
- §4 Non-flat descent. The annotations mention applications, including one to the flatness of a coherent module relative to something, and a lemma (name hard to read, probably Nakayama).
- §5 Non-flat quotients, i.e. passage to quotients in general.
- §6 Descent of étale relative schemes, possibly also descent of étale sheaves. This is the theme of SGA 1 IX and SGA 4 VIII on descent for étale objects along universally submersive or proper surjective maps.

Part B began as 'Propriétés générales des foncteurs sur (Sch)/S', crossed out and retitled 'Méthodes non projectives de construction'. These are construction methods that avoid FGA's Hilbert-scheme-and-projective-embedding route:
- §7 Pro-representability and variants. This is the Grothendieck–Schlessinger formal theory of moduli.
- §9 Differential invariants: tangent and normal spaces of functors, deformation and obstruction data.
- §10 General properties of functors and permanence properties, with the suggestion to place it 'after §12'. A brace attaches 'Foncteurs excellents sur S, morphismes excellents ??', which seems to propose an 'excellent' class of functors or morphisms stable under the usual operations.
- §11 Elementary representability results of the type Π_{X/Y} (Weil restriction) and Hom/Isom-type functors, referring to SGA 3 VIII 6 and XI 6.8. A boxed query reads 'Commencer ici ? Cas Grassmann(?) ?'.
- §8 Construction of coherent modules. This means producing coherent sheaves from compatible systems, i.e. algebraization and Grothendieck existence (EGA III 5), as an input to representability.
- §12 Functors represented by separated morphisms locally of finite presentation.
- §13 Applications: relative representability theorems, including for étale functors.

Part B as a whole is a programme for representability criteria in which a functor that is locally of finite presentation, has a pro-representable formal theory with controlled differential invariants and effective formal objects, and satisfies permanence properties becomes representable by a scheme locally of finite presentation. This is essentially the problem solved by M. Artin (1969–70) via Artin approximation, with algebraic spaces as the representing objects.
errors: The section numbering is in flux (§8 is placed after §11; §7 appears twice, the first crossed out; §10 is marked 'Après §12 ??'), but there is no mathematical error.

§12 implicitly hopes for representability by schemes. The later theory (Artin) shows that non-projective methods in general yield only algebraic spaces, so as stated §12 is too optimistic unless extra hypotheses are added. This is a plan, not a claim.

missed.claim: Grothendieck planned a full EGA chapter of 'non-projective methods of construction': pro-representability plus differential invariants plus permanence properties plus coherent-module construction leading to representability by schemes locally of finite presentation. This is essentially the programme Artin completed with algebraic spaces. It documents that Grothendieck himself intended a general representability theorem in EGA.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it situates Artin's criteria as answering a problem on Grothendieck's EGA agenda. This is mostly known in outline, but the explicit plan is a useful documentary source.

missed.claim: A tentative notion of 'excellent functors on S' and 'excellent morphisms', tied to permanence properties of functors, which never appeared in this form.
missed.quote: Foncteurs excellents sur S morphismes excellents ??
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may anticipate axiomatizing classes of functors stable under the operations needed for representability, akin to later work on Artin's axioms by Hall–Rydh and others. But the page gives no content beyond the name.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a plan page. Its interest lies in documenting that EGA VI was to include a non-projective representability theory, prefiguring Artin's work, plus a vague 'excellent functors' notion. There is no worked mathematics, and the overall intention is broadly known to historians.
